note: a colour key drag merges set steps on another frame
anchor: guard (next.owner, next.layerID, next.target, next.frame) == (owner, layerID, target, frame) else { return false }
replacement: guard (next.owner, next.layerID, next.target) == (owner, layerID, target) else { return false }

note: a colour key move clamps each key into the duration instead of refusing all
anchor: guard !overflow, to >= 0, to <= duration else { throw CommandError.invalidFrame(k.frame) }
replacement: guard !overflow, to >= 0, to <= duration else { k.frame = min(max(to, 0), duration); moved.append(k); continue }

note: a colour key move leaves the track keys unsorted
a colour key move that would leave the duration is dropped silently instead of refusing all
anchor: guard !overflow, to >= 0, to <= duration else { throw CommandError.invalidFrame(k.frame) }
replacement: guard !overflow, to >= 0, to <= duration else { continue }

note: a colour key set refuses the last frame of the scene
anchor: guard key.frame >= 0, key.frame <= duration else { throw CommandError.invalidFrame(key.frame) }
replacement: guard key.frame >= 0, key.frame < duration else { throw CommandError.invalidFrame(key.frame) }

note: a colour key move refuses landing on the last frame of the scene
a colour key move onto a key that stays is not refused as frameOccupied
a colour key set skips its invalidColor check on a NaN or out of range colour
a colour command skips its shapeNotFound check on a missing shape
a colour command reports a missing text target as a missing shape
anchor: if case .text(let index) = target { throw CommandError.invalidIndex(index) }

note: a colour key remove leaves an empty track instead of dropping it
a colour key remove at a frame with no key succeeds instead of keyframeNotFound
